question.text: Isobutyraldehyde on reaction with formaldehyde and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi>CO</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> gives compound '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>'. Compound '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>' reacts with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>KCN</mi></math> and yields compound '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math>', which on hydrolysis gives a stable compound '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>'. solution.text: In the first step formaldehyde undergoes cross aldol reaction with isobutyraldehyde to form  (A)and then the product(A) forms cyanohydrin (B)with KCN, which on hydrolysis forms a compound containing carboxylic acid group and finally this molecule undergoes intramolecular esterification to form (C) a stable compound.
